Bridge Retrofit Engineer said about it: Moving first mode from 1.9 Hz to 2.3 Hz needs 46.5 percent more bending stiffness from the stiffness-increase calculation (E27), and to 2.5 Hz needs 73.1 percent more from the higher-target calculation (E28), while 1.9 Hz sits inside the 1.25 to 2.3 Hz critical vertical range reported in the Human-Induced Vibration on Lightweight Footbridges — 2024 (E19) and the comfort-class review in the Microsoft Word - IJLCPE010105 VENUTI_no downsample.doc (E18).
Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor said about it: In plain words the bridge will resonate with normal walking so Maximum comfort is below 0.5 metres per second squared, Medium comfort is 0.5 to 1.0 metres per second squared, Minimum comfort is 1.0 to 2.5 metres per second squared and Unacceptable is above 2.5 metres per second squared, which is the band stated in the Low-Cost Angular-Velocity Measurements for Sustainable Dynamic Identification of Pedestrian Footbridges: A Case Study of the Footbridge in Gdynia (Poland) (E33) and in the comfort-target concept (C13), while 1.9 Hz falling inside the 1.25 to 2.3 Hz critical vertical range is stated in the Human-Induced Vibration on Lightweight Footbridges — 2024 (E19).
Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor said about it: I take from the Human-Induced Vibration on Lightweight Footbridges — 2024 (E19) that 1.9 Hz falls inside the 1.25 to 2.3 Hz critical vertical range, and I hold Maximum comfort below 0.5 m/s2, Medium comfort 0.5 to 1.0 m/s2, Minimum comfort 1.0 to 2.5 m/s2 and Unacceptable above 2.5 m/s2 from the comfort-target concept (C13) backed by the Low-Cost Angular-Velocity Measurements for Sustainable Dynamic Identification of Pedestrian Footbridges: A Case Study of the Footbridge in Gdynia (Poland) (E33).
